s.t: Mavis Staples worried that ‘If You’re Ready (Come Go with Me)’ was too close to The Staple Singers’ last hit, and the group hesitated before recording it.
s.q: Even within the group, there was hesitation. Mavis worried the song was too close to their last hit.

s.t: Homer Banks, Raymond Jackson and Carl Hampton wrote ‘If You’re Ready (Come Go with Me)’, which The Staple Singers took to number one on the R&B chart for three weeks.
s.q: Written by Homer Banks, Raymond Jackson, and Carl Hampton

s.t: In 1985 the British Jamaican singer Ruby Turner covered The Staple Singers’ song with the South African guitarist Jonathan Butler, reaching number three in New Zealand.
s.src: Wikipedia: If You're Ready (Come Go with Me)
s.q: In 1985, British Jamaican singer Ruby Turner covered  this song featuring South African singer-songwriter and guitarist Jonathan Butler.  Her version reached #30 in the UK, #29 in Ireland and number three in New Zealand.

s.t: The Australian singer Wendy Matthews covered The Staple Singers’ song on her 1991 live album The Way It Has to Be, and Steve Archer recorded it in 1987.
s.src: Wikipedia: If You're Ready (Come Go with Me)
s.q: In 1987, American Contemporary Christian singer Steve Archer covered this song for his fourth solo album Off the Page. In 1991, Australian singler Wendy Matthews covered it on her live album, The Way It Has to Be

f.t: Bob Dylan said in 2015 that their ‘Uncloudy Day’ was “the most mysterious thing I’d ever heard”, and that Mavis Staples’s singing “just knocked me out”.
f.q: “Uncloudy Day” was an early influence on Bob Dylan, who said of it in 2015, "It was the most mysterious thing I'd ever heard ... Her singing just knocked me out

f.t: Their father, Roebuck “Pops” Staples, worked in Chicago steel mills and meatpacking plants while the children grew up, and the family began singing in Chicago churches in 1948.
f.q: Roebuck worked in steel mills and meatpacking plants while his family of four children grew up. The family began appearing in Chicago-area churches in 1948.

f.t: At Stax, producer Al Bell had the rhythm sessions cut at Muscle Shoals Sound Studio, then added overdubs himself with engineer Terry Manning at Ardent Studios in Memphis.
f.q: Al Bell produced their recordings, conducting the rhythm sessions at the famed Muscle Shoals Sound Studio and cutting the overdubs himself with engineer/musician Terry Manning at Memphis's Ardent Studios

f.t: They performed ‘The Weight’ with The Band for The Band’s film The Last Waltz in 1976, having already covered it on their first Stax album.
f.q: In 1976, they collaborated with The Band for their film The Last Waltz, performing on the song "The Weight" (which The Staple Singers had previously covered on their first Stax album).
